video_title: Stephen A.'s MESSAGE for Shai Gilgeous-Alexander 🗣️ PROVE YOU'RE REALLY THE MVP! | First Take

quotes.speaker: Michael Wilbon
quotes.summary_phrase: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander must perform early in Game 2 as the MVP
quotes.excerpt: This is about Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. If he's going to be sort of that player we talk about...
quotes.quote: Very concerned because I got to win Game 2. I mean, I'm not concerned about the previous series and what he did or didn't do against the Lakers when it didn't matter. It matters now. It matters now, you're the two-time MVP. He got involved and really got engaged, activated in the fourth quarter last night. Too late in that game. But I mean, I don't want to overreact to the Game 1 loss. And he is the MVP and he has been a great player in the postseason. But this has to start in Game 2 and has to start early. He needs one of those games that is likely a 35 to 40 plus game. We don't know if Jalen Williams, we don't know how effective he is. They were working on both hamstrings at various points during the game. Chet's going to have his hands full with Victor Wembanyama no matter how effective he is or isn't in Game 2. This is about Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. If he's going to be sort of that player we talk about to have multiple championships and we're talking about who the league benefits from most if they win. This is Shai's time in Game 2 early and often.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Victor Wembanyama sent a message challenging Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's MVP title
quotes.excerpt: That trophy belongs to me. I don't believe you deserve it. I deserve it.
quotes.quote: Here's the part about Shai Gilgeous-Alexander. Do you remember what I said about Chet Holmgren in the first part of this show? Where's your pride? Where's your dignity? Are you going to stand by and let dudes a half an inch, a foot shorter than you guard Wembanyama when you're 7 feet 1? When are you going to embrace the challenge? Handle your business. You know what I'm saying? You ain't a scrub, you can play, do it. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is the reigning two-time league MVP. He hoisted that trophy last night. If you go back to the archives, Shai, you remember this. In the beginning of the season, Wilbon, Cam'ron, I went on the air and I said, could you imagine if Shai Gilgeous-Alexander won the league MVP again and San Antonio was facing them in the conference finals because we all know that's when you get the that's when you get the trophy. You understand? Usually when you're in the conference finals, they delay it and giving it to you until then. And I said, and he gets the trophy and Wembanyama is standing right there believing that it's something that belongs to him. Could you imagine that? Let's see Shai against Wemby in that scenario. Well, Wemby showed up. And Wemby seemed to be making the kind of statement to the voters, which I am one of them, where he was saying, y'all made the wrong choice. How were y'all thinking? That trophy belongs to me. Shai, butter, what are you going to do about that? What are you going to do about that? Because San Antonio is here and they're coming to take what you are the reigning defending NBA champions. And San Antonio in four or five meetings this year, beat you and then shows up to Game 1 on your home court without its star starting point guard and De'Aaron Fox and beat you again. That's five of six meetings. You're OKC. What are you going to do about it? Because they're coming. They're here. And they're letting you know they're coming to take what you have. You're right, go ahead, fine. Take that league MVP trophy that I don't believe you deserve. This is Wemby talking. I don't believe you deserve it. I deserve it. But go ahead and have that. I'm going to take your title from you. All right? I'm going to send you home and I'm going to win the chip. And I'm going to come back for that MVP next year. That's the message that Wemby sent last night.

quotes.speaker: Michael Wilbon
quotes.summary_phrase: Wembanyama's ruthless personality contrasts with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's quiet style
quotes.excerpt: Wembanyama seems personally ruthless. There seems to be a potentially a petty element to it sometimes.

text_blocks.speaker: Michael Wilbon
text_blocks.text: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander has been the quietest superstar you can really imagine. But he's also been a wonderful face for that organization. No doubt. He's going to have to make some noise in Game 2. You know, I just wonder when you you look you draw some distinctions between their personalities, those two guys. And Shai, who was what? 27, maybe turning 28 soon. He's still young enough where he's going to be in the ring against Wembanyama for a while. And there's this thing that Wembanyama has, this heat that you see that people do not seem offended by, maybe because he's still new to the scene. And I've been saying all season that Oklahoma City as a team is politely ruthless. They they have come to get you and to crush you. They've crushed certain teams all year. But Wembanyama seems personally ruthless. There seems to be a potentially a petty element to it sometimes, like he enjoys getting into it. Wembanyama's got a ruthlessness that we saw last night and it's like, wow. Wow. Does Shai have this? Is it necessary? Do you have to have that to sort of ascend and be opposite his number, Wembanyama's number, in these coming years? And it sets up. I mean, does it have to be somebody else? Is it going to be D'Antoni? Is it going to be Caleb Wilson? Is it going to be somebody from outside the picture frame right now who steps into it? Or are we going to get several installations of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Wembanyama?

text_blocks.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
text_blocks.text: You're going to have to make some noise now. Absolutely.

quotes.speaker: Cam'ron
quotes.summary_phrase: Spurs' defense will smother Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, forcing him to be Superman
quotes.excerpt: The defense that they're showing Shai, it's not that he's not making the right basketball play, they're going to smother him.
quotes.quote: Listen, Shai's going to have to step up, but I want to give some love to my man Sean Sweeney. We gave Miss Johnson his flowers. Sean Sweeney came from Dallas, got there this year and had the Spurs the third overall defense. The looks that they were showing given Shai, that's why I gave Mark Daigneault credit too. They had to send Lu Dort and Jalen Williams, whoever played Alex Caruso, Dan, all the way down the court to get Shai some space. So the defense that they're showing Shai, it's not that he's not making the right basketball play, they're going to smother him. The scout report is going to say that Alex Caruso is going to have to beat us every single game and Shai's going to be smothered from Game 1 through 4, 1 through 7, whatever it is. He did a great job in the second half and overtime, but he's going to face that this whole series. So I don't know if he's going to get better, but he's going to have to be Superman. So I wanted to give my man Sean Sweeney some love for the looks that he gave.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Oklahoma City must win now against San Antonio or risk never reaching the NBA Finals again
quotes.excerpt: If you don't knock them off now, you may never see another NBA Finals.
quotes.quote: We talk about Wemby coming and the San Antonio Spurs and the supporting cast that he has, they're being here. Here's where the level of urgency needs to kick in. San Antonio, you look at everybody, 22 years and younger. They got like the key nucleus of their team, like five or six dudes that's younger that that that that's 22 years or younger. They're not going away. They're trying to kick down the door to claim something Oklahoma City has with no intentions of giving it back in the foreseeable future. So there's a level of urgency that everybody in the league has to have. But especially OKC, because here's why. Can it get any better than the situation that Oklahoma City has right now? You have the reigning two-time league MVP as your star. You got a cat in Jaylen Williams, J-Dub, where he and Evan Mobley a couple of years ago were the only two dudes that made All-NBA plus an All-NBA Defensive Team. Okay? You got two seven-footers in Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein. All right? You got AJ Mitchell and Cason Wallace and these brothers who can play. And on top of it all, between now and 2032, over the next six years, the Oklahoma City Thunder have 13 first-round picks and 16 second-round picks. And it is very possible that with everything that I just laid out, because of this dude in Victor Wembanyama and these dudes in the San Antonio Spurs, that if you don't knock them off now, you may never see another NBA Finals. Because they are in your conference standing in your way and letting you know they are taking it personal and they are coming for you. As smooth and silk and as cool as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is, this ain't the time for that. You got to be loud, you got to be demonstrative, you've got to be emphatic. You've got to come and say, I'm not giving it up. You're going to have to come take it because I'm not giving it to you. We ain't going out like that. He's got to do it. And Chet Holmgren has to help him along with everybody else. Because San Antonio ain't messing around. They ain't messing around.

quotes.speaker: Stephen A. Smith
quotes.summary_phrase: Healthy OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges must perform for the Knicks
quotes.excerpt: Mikal Bridges has to be that guy because we know Donovan Mitchell might get loose.
quotes.quote: Well, it's two people that come to my mind. I know I'm supposed to give one but I'm going to give two only because one is involving injury. I need to see OG Anunoby healthy. After being out with the in the Sixers series with the hamstring injury and whatever the last few games, I want to see him back healthy. The fact that he's gotten this rest, that they got this break because they swept the Sixers and Cleveland and Detroit went seven games. I think it's incredibly important that this guy is in the flow. Remember, he was shooting better than 60% from the field and better than 50% from three-point range, averaging over 20 when he went down in the playoffs. So we have to understand his importance. Strictly in regards to their performance more so than anything else, I'm going to say the name Mikal Bridges again. I'm going to say again. Yes, Wilbon, you're absolutely right. It ain't his fault that all them damn draft picks were given up for him. It ain't his fault. I got it, but damn it, they were given up. Okay? And this is the Knicks, I mean, this is the Knicks situation. And it's going to stay this way for the foreseeable future because they gave up all of these assets. He has to justify it. And he doesn't have to do anything more than he's been doing over the last few games in these playoffs since they blew out Atlanta by 50 in the first half of Game or the close out Game 6. You know, so he's been flowing ever since. Keep that up, is all I'm trying to say. Mikal Bridges has to be that guy because we know Donovan Mitchell might get loose, who knows what James Harden is going to do, who knows what Jarrett Allen and Evan Mobley are going to do. But I'm going to say the name that comes to my mind is Mikal Bridges. If OG Anunoby is healthy and Mikal Bridges is balling, the New York Knicks are easily going to win this series.

quotes.speaker: Cam'ron
quotes.summary_phrase: Karl-Anthony Towns and Jarrett Allen must overcome past playoff struggles
quotes.excerpt: The lights are going to be brighter than three years ago. You're going to have to step up this year.
quotes.quote: I'll give you one from each team. I'm going to say for the New York Knicks it has to be Karl-Anthony Towns. Last series, we seen him basically play with a handicap when we're talking about Joel Embiid. You got to sag off him on defense. Therefore helped you out defensively when you seen screens coming, people cutting through, etc. because he was hobbled on defense. Not just that, offensively when they were, we'll call him point center cat, had the ball in his hands, when he got the drive, defense also collapsed on him. So you're able to find open shots from Jalen Brunson, Mikal Bridges and where the Knicks just shot lights out, 57% from three-point land. And that was the key to that. You are, you know, you're a big handicap because of Joel Embiid. Are you going to do that against Evan Mobley? We'll see that. And on the other side of the ball, I'll say, it has to be Jarrett Allen. He had two great sensational Game 7s in this playoff so far. But I remember him a couple years ago and your guy Wendy actually brought it up, how he got smoked by Mitchell Robinson. And he said the lights were too bright for him. And that was three years ago. The lights are going to be brighter than three years ago. And you've been playing exceptionally well this series. You're going to have to step up this year for the Cleveland Cavaliers to have a chance.

quotes.speaker: Michael Wilbon
quotes.summary_phrase: Donovan Mitchell's early assertiveness is crucial for the Cavaliers to relieve pressure on James Harden
quotes.excerpt: Donovan Mitchell is assertive and productive early, it takes a lot of the pressure off James Harden.
quotes.quote: I don't disagree with any of those. Those are those are key people and more than one person has to show up big in any playoff game, particularly a conference finals playoff game. I'll stick with Cleveland for a second. And it's going to be Donovan Mitchell. Look, Donovan Mitchell is capable of 50 point games in the playoffs. We know that. He doesn't have to have that tonight. I'm not suggesting he needs to be some great soloist. But here's what it does if Donovan Mitchell is assertive and productive early, it takes a lot of the pressure off James Harden. Stephen A, you and I particularly have spent a lot of years chronicling and having to be critical in the playoffs, particularly as mid-May turns to late May of James Harden and what he hasn't done. But what James Harden can do particularly if Donovan Mitchell is taking the pressure off him scoring, James Harden can just go to facilitation mode. He can do that and have 10, 11, 12 assists and be incredibly effective. This is not a situation where James Harden has to be what he was in Houston and has to come out and have a 35 point, 15 assist game. No, he doesn't need to do that. But in order to sort of settle into that role, you need Donovan Mitchell scoring a lot in this game. And it also, you know, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen can then follow suit. Somebody's got to set the tone for Cleveland. Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen, you can't have any 3.2 assist, two rebound games out of them. They need bigger games. We saw that late in the Toronto series, we saw it late in the Detroit series. They can't wait till late. Otherwise, there won't be a late in the Knicks series if they don't get started and preferably tonight.
